facts.statement: The species name of this extinct waterfowl is Bambolinetta lignitifila.
The genus Bambolinetta was established by Mayr and Pavia in 2014.
Fossils of Bambolinetta date to the Late Miocene epoch.
The species was originally described by Portis in 1884.
Bambolinetta lignitifila is a fossil waterfowl species found in Late Miocene deposits in Italy.
facts.quote: Bambolinetta lignitifila is a fossil species of waterfowl from the Late Miocene of Italy

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Bambolinetta is a partial skeleton collected in Montebamboli, Tuscany.
facts.quote: The species is known from partial skeleton collected in Montebamboli, Tuscany

facts.statement: Alessandro Portis formally described the species in 1884 under the name Anas lignitifila.
facts.quote: The species was formally described by Alessandro Portis in 1884, with the name Anas lignitifila

facts.statement: Gerald Mayr and Marco Pavia conducted the first reexamination of the species in a 2014 paper.
facts.quote: The first reexamination of the species was made in a paper by Gerald Mayr and Marco Pavia published in 2014

facts.statement: A 2014 study reclassified the species as a highly unusual, likely flightless, wing-propelled diver similar to a penguin.
facts.quote: it was not revisited until 2014, when a study showed it to be a highly unusual duck species, probably a flightless, wing-propelled diver similar to a penguin

facts.statement: Mayr and Pavia placed the species in its own genus named Bambolinetta based on its type locality.
facts.quote: Accordingly, they placed the species in its own genus, taking the name Bambolinetta from its type locality

facts.statement: The sole specimen consists of a partial skeleton including an incomplete skull, most of the trunk, a right wing, and parts of the leg bones.
facts.quote: The sole specimen of the species consists of a partial skeleton on a slab, that includes an incomplete skull, most of the trunk, right wing, parts of the tibiotarsus and tarsometatarsus

facts.statement: Bambolinetta was likely mid-sized for a duck during its life.
facts.quote: This species was probably mid-sized for a duck in life

facts.statement: The species possessed arm bones, particularly the humerus, that were much stouter than those of any other ducks.
facts.quote: had arm bones, in particular the humerus, that are much stouter than those of any other anatids

facts.statement: The ulna was short relative to the humerus and hand, a feature shared with auks and penguins.
facts.quote: The ulna is short relative to the humerus and hand, as in auks and penguins

facts.statement: The region where Bambolinetta lived formed the Tusco-Sardinian island during the Late Miocene.
facts.quote: the region that it lived in formed the Tusco-Sardinian island

facts.statement: The parent group of Bambolinetta is the subfamily Anatinae.
Bambolinetta belongs to the family Anatidae.
The time range for Bambolinetta is the Aquitanian stage, from 23.04 to 20.45 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aquitanian to Aquitanian (23.04 to 20.45 million years ago)
